title: DrawIO Export
description: Structured JSON representation of a .drawio file with full round-trip fidelity.

host.description: Value of the host attribute on the <mxfile> root element

diagrams.description: One entry per <diagram> page in the file

graph_model.description: All attributes of <mxGraphModel> (dx, dy, grid, pageWidth, …)

cells.description: All <mxCell> and <object>/<mxCell> elements in flat order

Cell.description: A single mxCell vertex, edge, or edge-label, possibly wrapped in an <object> element.

id.description: Unique cell identifier within the diagram. Use make_id() from drawio_codec to generate UUIDs for programmatically created cells.

value.description: Label text (may contain HTML). For object-wrapped cells this is the <object label='...'> attribute.

parent.description: ID of the parent cell (builds the containment hierarchy)

vertex.description: Present with value '1' when the cell is a vertex (shape)

edge.description: Present with value '1' when the cell is an edge (connector)

source.description: Source vertex ID for edge cells

target.description: Target vertex ID for edge cells

object_attrs.description: Extra attributes from an enclosing <object> element (e.g. C4 metadata: c4Name, c4Type, placeholders…)

additionalProperties.description: Any other mxCell XML attribute preserved verbatim (e.g. connectable, visible, tooltip)
Any unknown future mxGeometry XML attribute (always a scalar — draw.io geometry attributes are never nested objects or arrays beyond the named properties above)

y.description: Top edge position (omitted when 0). Always omitted for shape=tableRow cells — their vertical position is managed by childLayout=tableLayout.

relative.description: Set on edge geometry to indicate relative positioning

offset.description: Offset for inline child shapes (e.g. edge decorators)

waypoints.description: Intermediate bend points for curved/orthogonal edges

alternate_bounds.description: Collapsed bounds stored in <mxRectangle as='alternateBounds'>. Only present when the bounds differ from the regular geometry width/height — identical alternate_bounds are stripped during parsing.
